Zuberi, M.J.S., Hasanbeigi, A. and Morrow, W. (2023). Techno-economic evaluation of industrial heat pump applications in US pulp and paper, textile, and automotive industries. Energy Efficiency 16(1), 19. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12053-023-10089-6

Loaded: 5 heat-pump types (HTHP 50/82/90 degC hot water; SGHP 120/150 degC steam) and one 27 degC air-source HP with printed COPs (as %), sink temperature, state of development, and the common IHP cost assumptions (capex 466.7 2021$/kW derived from the stated ~$7 bn for ~15 GW; O&M 1%/yr; lifetime 15 yr; discount rate 10%); for each of four processes (Tables 1-4) the IHP electricity per t product and the conventional boiler fuel per t product with the boiler efficiency (80/80/75/82%). Projections sidecar: 2050 CO2 abatement costs per sector. In _other-values: the printed capex curve y = 1186.2x^-0.113 and evaluated points, national capacities, cost of conserved energy ($/GJ-saved), production volumes, emission factors. Not available: capacity factor, levelized cost of heat, 2021 abatement costs (charts only).

(1) Capex is a curve over capacity; the single loaded value is an average derived from rounded totals ('approximately $7 billion', '15 GW'). (2) Sector capacities printed in the text sum to ~13.1 GW (0.15 + 0.012 + 0.375 + 6.8 + 5.8), not the 15 GW used in the abstract/conclusions. (3) Eq. 2 is printed as Tsink/(Tsource - Tsink), sign inverted; Eq. 3 body is missing in the text layer. (4) Table 3 total boiler fuel 3027.8 kWh/t vs sum of rows 3015.1; Table 4 modified fuel total 6.4 GJ/t (1785.1 kWh/t) vs rows 6.5 (1771.6); Table 2 boiler-fuel GJ rows sum 27.8 vs total 27.6. (5) Table 1: 10.5 GJ/t printed as 2907.5 kWh/t (10.5 GJ = 2916.7 kWh). (6) Automotive HTHP 1 COP printed as 6 at '~50 degC' (method gives ~5.8). (7) Boiler fuel is not named; natural gas is implied only by Eqs 5 and 8. Capex price year taken from the Fig. 1 axis label (2021 $/kW). (8) Sensitivity text says electricity prices 'taken 1.5 times lower' but Figs 6/10 notes say 50% lower.
